podcast.title: Audition for Sam Phillips and Reduction to The Tennessee 3
podcast.body: Johnny Cash brought Luther Perkins, Marshall Grant, and Red Carnotle to meet Sam Phillips. When it came time to audition, the steel player, Red Carnotle, became so nervous he couldn't tune his guitar and decided to leave, feeling he was holding the others back. The remaining trio became "The Tennessee 3," a name they chose because, though they all lived in Tennessee, none were originally from there. "Eventually he decided that he was holding the other three back, and left the studio, and the audition continued with just the group who had now become the Tennessee 3."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Formation and Early Sound
podcast.body: The group initially formed as Johnny Cash, Luther Perkins, and Marshall Grant, sometimes including steel player Red Carnotle. They were unskilled but possessed a willingness to experiment and Cash's distinctive voice. They primarily played gospel songs, aiming to sound like The Louvin Brothers. "Cash, Perkins and Grant all played acoustic guitar at first, and none of them were particularly good."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Musical Limitations and Innovative Sound
podcast.body: Their limitations as musicians forced them to develop a unique sound. Luther Perkins played electric guitar lead lines that were essentially boogie-woogie bass lines transposed up an octave. Marshall Grant, who had never played double bass before, taped markers on his instrument and could only play single notes on every other beat, creating big gaps. These limitations paradoxically led to their signature sound, focusing on rhythm rather than virtuosity. "Their limitations as musicians meant that they had to find ways to make the songs work without relying on complicated parts of virtuoso playing."
